question.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $(3x)(7y)$ in the numerator becomes $3\cdot 7\cdot x\cdot y,$ and the $28y$ in the denominator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 7\cdot y.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{(3x)(7y)}{28y}=\frac{3\cdot 7\cdot x\cdot y}{2\cdot 2\cdot 7\cdot y}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $7\text{'s}$ and one pair of $y$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{3\cdot 7\cdot x\cdot y}{2\cdot 2\cdot 7\cdot y} & = \\ \frac{3\cdot \cancel{7}\cdot x\cdot \cancel{y}}{2\cdot 2\cdot \cancel{7}\cdot \cancel{y}} & = \\ \frac{3\cdot x}{2\cdot 2} & = \\ \frac{3}{4}x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{3}{4}x.$
